title: content/perk_draft/perk_draft.json
description: M7-07 — the loc keys the Perk Draft screen (S07) renders. What is fixed here is that the screen heads the draft; labels a synergy hint, the reroll's price and the skip's reward; carries the one translated word an upgrade badge is composed from; offers a reroll and a skip; carries the one sentence a guarantee row needs when it cannot count; and carries one status line per state the read, the projection and a submission can be in. Every value is a loc key, so the content build resolves it against every locale file: a key this document names but a locale does not carry fails the build, and a locale string this document stops naming fails it as an orphan. additionalProperties is false on every object so the absences are enforced rather than merely observed. The three DRAFT guarantee captions in label are a store-policy requirement rather than a nicety — 24 §1.1 requires every luck-protection counter shown always with a real number, and every N in §4 stated on its class's own screen. There is no member for a remaining-free-reroll count or for a per-draft cap, because neither exists in the rules layer at all — the reroll charges Gold on every call, with no counter and no ceiling, so a count drawn here would be a number nothing could compute. There is no member for anything ad-shaped — no ad reroll, no fourth card by ad, no placement, cap or reward — because the ad reward command is not built and a screen naming one advertises a feature the game does not have. And there is no member carrying a MAGNITUDE: the reroll's price, the skip's reward and every perk effect number are tunables read at render time and drawn beside the captions here, because a number written into a translated string cannot be tuned and would be wrong in two languages at once.

locKey.description: loc.<domain>.<id>.<field>, lowercase, dot-separated, snake_case segments — the same shape schema/loc.schema.json governs the locale files by.

name.description: The screen's own heading, and nothing else: the three cards carry the perk catalogue's names, and there is no fourth card to caption because the ad that would earn one is not built.

label.description: 🔒 Captions only, and that is the rule this object exists to keep. REQUIRED, all six: the three DRAFT guarantee captions are not optional decoration but 24 §1.1's Visibility rule, which is a 🔒 — every luck-protection counter is shown to the player ALWAYS, as a plain sentence with a real number, because a hidden pity system is indistinguishable from no pity system — together with its Disclosure rule, which makes stating every N in §4 on its class's own screen a store-policy requirement on both platforms. DRAFT is the class (§3) and S07 is the screen, so a build that dropped one of these three captions would ship a screen out of compliance, and required is what makes that a build failure instead of a missing row. Exactly three, because only three of §4.7's five rules count anything: the Sustain anti-brick is a state predicate and the Codex bias is a weight. rerollCost and skipReward are the words a number is drawn BESIDE — the price and the reward are authored tunables read through the draft economy, and one of them is flagged in its own document as a placeholder for the balance team. A magnitude written into either of these strings would be untunable, would have to be corrected in every locale at once, and would disagree with the rules layer the first time the balance changed. synergy leads in the hint naming which owned perks an option interacts with.

badge.description: The one translated part of a tier badge. A fresh card's badge is a tier numeral and nothing else, which is the same mark in every language; an upgrade's badge is this word followed by the numeral the option lands on. Composed on the client rather than authored whole, because a badge authored as finished English would be a user-facing string produced outside the loc system.

action.description: Every control the screen offers, and both are built: the reroll charges Gold, and the skip is the only way off this screen that costs the player nothing, so its caption going missing is a run that cannot read its way out of a draft. No ad reroll is captioned, because none exists to press.

block.description: 🔒 The one sentence on this screen about something that is not there, and it is about a mechanic that IS built. The upgrade famine is live and enforced, and simply cannot be owed by a run holding no perk below its top tier — so its row shows its authored rung with no countdown, and guaranteeNotDue says why, because a rung with no countdown and no reason reads as a counter that has stopped working. Nothing else here gets a sentence: an ad reroll, a fourth card by ad or a free-reroll allowance would each be a sentence about a feature the game does not have, and a player reading one waits for a feature when they should be earning Gold or drafting a perk.

status.description: One line per state the screen can be in with nothing to choose from, plus the three answers a submission can come back with. cardsUnavailable is a draft that is genuinely open whose cards the content set could not project — three blank cards and no explanation looks exactly like a draft the player is expected to choose from. effectNumbersUnavailable stands in for one card's effect sentence when that perk's authored description names a token its own effect data cannot answer; a renderer filling the hole would state a magnitude the game does not have on a card a run is about to be committed to. rerollUnaffordable is separated from refused because a shortfall is the one refusal here a player can act on, and it is paired with the reroll so it is never printed under a command that spends nothing.
